라면.x: I was hungry, so I made ramyeon.
라면.e: From Japanese 'ramen' — but in Korea it usually means instant noodles.
라면.t: You 'boil' ramyeon in Korean: 라면을 끓이다.

포도.x: I bought grapes at the market.
포도.e: Sino-Korean, but the syllables have no separate meaning. 포도주 = wine ('grape alcohol').
포도.t: For wine, 와인 is also common.

사전.x: I look up words I don't know in the dictionary.
사전.e: Literally 'words reference book'. 영한사전 = English-Korean dictionary.
사전.t: Homonym: 사전 (事前) also means 'beforehand', as in 사전 예약.

전화번호.t: Phone numbers use Sino-Korean digits; 0 is 공: 010 = 공일공.

알다.forms: 알아요 · 알았어요 · 알 거예요 · 아세요 (ㄹ drops)
알다.x: Do you know that person's phone number?
알다.t: 알겠어요 / 알겠습니다 = 'Got it, understood.' 알았어요 is also used this way.

시원하다.ex: 더운 날에는 시원한 물을 마시고 싶어요.
시원하다.x: On hot days I want to drink cool water.
시원하다.e: Koreans also say 시원하다 after a good massage.
시원하다.t: Koreans also say 시원해요 about hot soup — meaning 'refreshing, satisfying'.

배부르다.x: I ate too much, so I'm full.
배부르다.t: 르 irregular: 배부르다 → 배불러요. Also said 배가 불러요.

진짜.forms: 진짜 + adjective/verb: 진짜 맛있어요; as a question: 진짜요?
진짜.t: More casual than 정말; very common in everyday speech.

커튼.x: When I open the curtains in the morning, sunlight comes in.
커튼.t: 커튼을 치다 = to draw the curtains closed; 커튼을 걷다 = to pull them open.

선배.ex: 학교 선배가 맛있는 밥을 사 줬어요.
선배.x: An upperclassman from school bought me a nice meal.
선배.e: Literally 'earlier generation' — someone who started before you.
선배.t: Based on who started first, not age; juniors often call them 선배님.

세금.ex: 월급에서 세금을 내고 나면 얼마 안 남아요.
세금.x: After paying taxes out of my salary, there isn't much left.

패션.x: My friend is really interested in fashion.
패션.e: From English 'fashion'; also in 패션쇼 'fashion show.'

배려하다.m: to be considerate of, to care about (others)
배려하다.ex: 제 친구는 항상 다른 사람을 배려해요.
배려하다.x: My friend is always considerate of others.
배려하다.e: Literally 'share out your concern' to others.
배려하다.t: Takes a direct object: 친구를 배려하다, not 친구에게.

결론.x: After a long meeting, we reached a conclusion.
결론.t: Pronounced [결론]; to reach a conclusion is 결론을 내리다.

변화하다.ex: 스마트폰 때문에 사람들의 생활이 많이 변화했어요.
변화하다.x: People's lives have changed a lot because of smartphones.
변화하다.t: More formal than 바뀌다 or 변하다; common in news and essays about society or trends.

사위.ex: 장인어른이 사위를 아주 마음에 들어 하세요.
사위.x: The father-in-law really likes his son-in-law.
사위.e: Pairs with 며느리 'daughter-in-law'; a 사위 calls his wife's parents 장인 and 장모.

보살피다.m: to take care of, to look after
보살피다.x: My older sister lovingly takes care of our sick mother.
보살피다.e: Probably 보다 'to look' + 살피다 'to watch closely': keeping a careful eye on someone.

배신.ex: 친한 친구의 배신 때문에 많이 힘들었어요.
배신.x: I had a really hard time because of a close friend's betrayal.

마주치다.m: to run into, bump into; (eyes) to meet
마주치다.x: I ran into a high school friend on the subway by chance.
마주치다.t: 눈이 마주치다 means 'to make eye contact', often by accident.

빌다.forms: 빌어요 · 빌었어요 · 빌 거예요 · 비세요 (ㄹ drops)
빌다.m: to wish, pray; to beg (for forgiveness)
빌다.ex: 생일 케이크 앞에서 눈을 감고 소원을 빌었어요.
빌다.x: I closed my eyes in front of my birthday cake and made a wish.
빌다.t: Don't confuse it with 빌리다 'to borrow'; 행운을 빌어요 means 'good luck'.

부대찌개.m: budae-jjigae (army stew with ham and sausage)
부대찌개.x: We add ramyeon noodles to our budae-jjigae.
부대찌개.e: 부대 'military unit' + 찌개 'stew'. It began after the Korean War with ham and sausages from US army bases.
부대찌개.t: Adding 라면 사리 (a block of instant noodles) is almost standard.

캠핑장.x: It's really hard to book a campground on weekends.
캠핑장.t: Popular campgrounds open online reservations at a set time and can be fully booked within minutes for summer weekends.

음매.x: A cow is mooing in the field.
음매.e: 의성어 (sound word) imitating the low call of a cow or calf.

말랑말랑.x: The freshly made rice cake is still soft and squishy.
말랑말랑.e: Manner word (의태어) for something soft and springy to the touch. Dark-vowel 물렁물렁 is softer and can sound mushy.
말랑말랑.t: Usually as 말랑말랑하다; the short form 말랑하다 is also common.

에 비해.forms: N에 비해(서) · N에 비하면 · -는 것에 비해
에 비해.ex: 이 식당은 가격에 비해 양이 많아요.
에 비해.x: This restaurant gives big portions for the price.
에 비해.t: Often means 'for' in judgments: 나이에 비해 어려 보여요 'You look young for your age.'

기고.m: contribution (of an article), contributed piece, op-ed
기고.ex: 그 교수는 신문에 환경에 관한 글을 기고했어요.
기고.x: The professor contributed an article on the environment to the newspaper.
기고.e: Literally 'sending a manuscript' to a publication.

대범하다.m: big-hearted, broad-minded; unfazed by small things
대범하다.ex: 그는 대범해서 작은 실수에는 신경 쓰지 않아요.
대범하다.x: He's easygoing about things, so he doesn't worry about small mistakes.
대범하다.e: Literally 'big and broad' — not bothered by little things.

허세.ex: 그는 친구들 앞에서 허세를 부리는 걸 좋아해요.
허세.x: He likes to put on a show in front of his friends.
허세.e: Literally 'empty power' — a show of strength with nothing behind it.
허세.t: Collocation: 허세를 부리다 means to put on airs or show off.

끌다.forms: 끌어요 · 끌었어요 · 끌 거예요 · 끄세요 (ㄹ drops)
끌다.m: to pull, to drag; to attract (attention); to drag out (time)
끌다.ex: 그 영화는 젊은 사람들의 관심을 끌었어요.
끌다.x: That movie attracted young people's attention.
끌다.t: Set phrases: 관심을 끌다 (attract interest), 시간을 끌다 (stall for time).

다가가다.m: to approach, to go up to
다가가다.e: 다가 'closer' + 가다 'to go'; with 오다 it becomes 다가오다 'to come closer'.

마주하다.m: to face, to sit facing; to confront
마주하다.ex: 두 사람이 테이블을 사이에 두고 마주했어요.
마주하다.x: The two of them faced each other across the table.

숨을 돌리다.forms: 숨을 돌려요 · 숨을 돌렸어요 · 한숨 돌리다
숨을 돌리다.m: to catch one's breath, to take a breather
숨을 돌리다.ex: 바쁜 일이 끝나서 이제 좀 숨을 돌릴 수 있어요.
숨을 돌리다.x: The busy stretch is over, so now I can catch my breath.
숨을 돌리다.e: Literally 'to get one's breath back' after rushing around.

관념.ex: 시간 관념이 없는 사람과 일하기는 힘들어요.
관념.x: It's hard to work with someone who has no sense of time.
관념.e: Literally 'viewing thought': how you picture something in your mind.
관념.t: 시간 관념 means a sense of punctuality; 고정관념 means a stereotype.

울퉁불퉁.x: The country road is bumpy, so the car shakes a lot.
울퉁불퉁.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a surface full of bumps and dips; the rhyme 울퉁 + 불퉁 echoes the up-and-down.
울퉁불퉁.t: Mostly used as 울퉁불퉁하다. Also for bulging muscles: 근육이 울퉁불퉁해요.

입법부.x: The National Assembly is the legislative branch that makes laws.
입법부.e: Literally 'law-making office'; 입법부, 사법부, 행정부 are the three branches.
입법부.t: Pronounced [입뻡뿌] — consonants after the ㅂ batchim become tense.

탈세.ex: 그 사업가는 탈세 혐의로 조사를 받고 있어요.
탈세.x: That businessman is being investigated on charges of tax evasion.
탈세.t: 탈세 is illegal evasion; 절세 is legally reducing your taxes.

신조.ex: 정직은 제가 평생 지켜 온 삶의 신조예요.
신조.x: Honesty is the creed I've lived by all my life.
신조.e: Literally 'articles of belief' — the rules you live by.

재현.ex: 이 마을은 조선 시대 생활을 그대로 재현했어요.
재현.x: This village recreates Joseon-era life exactly as it was.
재현.t: 재현 recreates a scene or result; 재연 re-performs something, like a crime reenactment.

유보하다.m: to reserve, to withhold (judgment, a decision)
유보하다.ex: 그는 그 문제에 대한 판단을 유보했습니다.
유보하다.x: He reserved judgment on the issue.
유보하다.e: Literally 'hold back and keep' — not deciding yet.

판별하다.m: to distinguish, to discern, to tell apart
판별하다.ex: 이 기계는 진짜 돈과 가짜 돈을 판별합니다.
판별하다.x: This machine tells real money from fake money.

갖추어지다.m: to be equipped, to be in place, to be ready
갖추어지다.ex: 이 아파트에는 편의 시설이 잘 갖추어져 있어요.
갖추어지다.x: This apartment complex is well equipped with amenities.
갖추어지다.e: 갖추다 'to equip' + -어지다 (passive); often shortened to 갖춰지다.

안일하다.m: complacent, careless, easygoing (in a bad way)
안일하다.ex: 정부의 안일한 대응이 피해를 더 키웠습니다.
안일하다.x: The government's complacent response made the damage worse.
안일하다.e: Literally 'ease and leisure' — too comfortable to take care.
안일하다.t: Common in news criticism: 안일한 대응 'complacent response', 안일한 생각 'naive, careless thinking'.

우유부단.ex: 그는 우유부단해서 메뉴 하나도 못 골라요.
우유부단.x: He's so indecisive he can't even pick a dish off the menu.
우유부단.e: Literally 'too gentle and soft to make the cut'.
우유부단.t: Usually 우유부단하다; it has nothing to do with 우유 'milk'.

사상누각.m: a castle built on sand; something without a solid foundation
사상누각.ex: 기초가 약하면 아무리 좋은 계획도 사상누각입니다.
사상누각.x: If the foundation is weak, even the best plan is a castle built on sand.

효험.ex: 할머니는 이 차가 감기에 효험이 있다고 하셨어요.
효험.x: Grandma said this tea works well for colds.
효험.t: 효험 sounds a bit old-fashioned; it's typical for folk remedies and traditional medicine.

취약 계층.ex: 정부는 취약 계층을 위한 지원을 늘렸습니다.
취약 계층.x: The government increased support for vulnerable groups.

수모.ex: 그는 많은 사람 앞에서 큰 수모를 당했어요.
수모.x: He suffered a great humiliation in front of many people.

미봉책.m: stopgap measure, makeshift fix, band-aid solution
미봉책.ex: 이번 대책은 근본적인 해결이 아닌 미봉책에 불과합니다.
미봉책.x: This measure is just a band-aid solution, not a fundamental fix.
미봉책.e: Literally 'a plan of patching and sewing up' a tear.
미봉책.t: Strongly critical in tone; often contrasted with 근본적인 해결책, a real solution.

분쟁지역.ex: 기자들은 위험을 무릅쓰고 분쟁지역에서 취재를 했습니다.
분쟁지역.x: Reporters risked danger to cover the news in the conflict zone.

계시.ex: 그는 꿈에서 신의 계시를 받았다고 주장했어요.
계시.x: He claimed he received a revelation from God in a dream.
계시.e: Literally 'opening up and showing' — a truth disclosed from above.

기술이전.ex: 두 나라는 기술이전에 관한 협정을 맺었습니다.
기술이전.x: The two countries signed an agreement on technology transfer.
기술이전.t: Pronounced [기수리전] — the final ㄹ links to the next vowel.

문예.m: literature and the arts; literary arts
문예.ex: 그는 대학 시절 문예 동아리에서 시를 썼어요.
문예.x: He wrote poems in a literary club in college.
문예.t: Pronounced [무녜]; common in compounds like 문예창작과 'creative writing department.'

민담.ex: 어릴 때 할머니께서 도깨비가 나오는 민담을 자주 들려주셨어요.
민담.x: When I was little, my grandmother often told me folktales with goblins in them.
민담.e: Literally 'people's tales' — stories told by ordinary folk.

누란지위.m: an extremely precarious situation, imminent danger
누란지위.x: At that time, the country was in an extremely precarious situation.

견지하다.m: to maintain, to hold firmly (a position or view)
견지하다.x: The government said it would maintain its existing position.

엄수하다.m: to strictly observe, to keep strictly (time, rules)
엄수하다.x: Please strictly observe the exam time.

피상적.ex: 피상적인 이해만으로는 이 문제를 해결할 수 없어요.
피상적.x: You can't solve this problem with only a superficial understanding.
피상적.e: Literally 'skin-appearance': looking only at the surface.

남발하다.m: to issue recklessly, to overuse, to throw around (promises)
남발하다.x: Politicians throw around campaign promises every election.
남발하다.e: Literally 'issue in excess', like printing too much money.

알선하다.m: to arrange, to mediate, to broker
알선하다.x: The school helps graduates find jobs.
알선하다.e: Literally 'turn and revolve': moving things around to connect two sides.
알선하다.t: Pronounced [알썬하다]. Neutral (취업 알선) or negative (불법 알선) depending on context.

버무리다.m: to mix, to toss (food with seasoning); to blend
버무리다.ex: 절인 배추를 고춧가루 양념에 골고루 버무려요.
버무리다.x: Toss the salted cabbage evenly in the red pepper seasoning.
버무리다.e: A kimchi-making verb — picture hands tossing cabbage in red seasoning.

타자.ex: 타자를 이해하려면 먼저 자신을 알아야 해요.
타자.x: To understand the other, you must first know yourself.
타자.t: Homonyms: 타자 also means 'batter' in baseball and 'typing'.
